paragraphs: Hoil veqayma lan: kol maqom sheaseru chakamim mippene marit haayin, apillu bechadre chadarim asur, al-ken, mi shennasheru kelayv bammayim, o apillu shennishpeku alehem mayim muatim o me geshamim, asur leshatecham mippene marit haayin, shello yachsheduhu shekkibsam beshabbat; vaapillu shotecham bechadre chadarim sheen roin sham – asur; mihu, lo aseru ella leshatecham beshabbat, abal im hayu shetuchim meereb shabbat, eno chayyab lesalleqan; veken lo yishtach adam kelayv beshabbat apillu min hazzea. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" heeleti besiyyata dishmayya: ha deameru "min hazzea" hu orecha demilleta, deen derek lishtoach ella im ken yesh bahem lachluchit mayim o lachluchit zea, deim hem yebeshim lamma yishtachem? abal in haki name leinyan dina, apillu im yebeshim asur leshatechan kederek sheshshotechin kelim hamkubbasim, mippene hachashad, deharoeh eno yodea shehem yebeshim; deiqqar gezerat chaza"l hu al hashsheticha, dibet sheroin oto shoteach beshabbat, choshedin oto shekkibsam beshabbat, dilkak im hayu shetuchim meereb shabbat eno chayyab lesalleqan, veyishshaaru shetuchim beshabbat, ki haggezera hi al et sheshshoteach; vaapillu shennireh habbeged merachoq shehu yabesh beet sheshshotecho, im kol zeh yachashod shennitlaklek qetzat mimmennu vekibbes hallikluk; velaken gam beged yabesh kullo legamre, asur leshatecho beshabbat kederek sheshshotechin kelim hamkubbasim, abal litloto al hachebel bilti sheticha, let lan bah.

Veod heeleti besiata dishmayya sham, deim abar veshatach begadayv beshabbat, "p sheasa issur en mechayyebin oto lesalleqam velahasiran, ki haggezera hayeta al hashsheticha ukebar asa haissur, sheshshatach veabar al dibre chaza"l, ulemay napeqa mina yesirem? ki bazeh lo yetaqqen hachashad dechashu lo chaza"l al et sheshshatach, deharoeh otam shettochin beshabbat, im lo raa otam sheshshetacham hayyom lo yabo lechashedo shekkibsam hayyom, deha hashshittuchin meereb shabbat eno chayyab lahasiram mippene chashad zeh. veim tomar: akkatti nachush shemma haadam raa biknisat shabbat et maqom zeh reqam, shello hayu bo kelim shetuchim, vechozer veroeh aach"k beshabbat kelim shettochin - yabo lachshod shekkibassem beshabbat; ulekak mechamat ken tzarik ligzor gam im abar veshatach beshabbat, chayyab lesalleqam velahasiram? zeh eno deen lanu ligzor gezerot chadashot middatenu, meachar digzerat chaza"l lo hayeta ella baabur chashad haroeh oto shoteach habbeged; velaken heeleti deim abar veshatach, en mechayyebin oto lahasiro.

clarification.explanation: Since anything the Sages forbade out of concern for appearances is forbidden even in a completely hidden place, one whose clothes became wet with water, or even had a little water or rainwater spilled on them, is forbidden to spread them out to dry on the Sabbath, out of concern that people will suspect he laundered them on the Sabbath, even if he spreads them in a hidden place where no one can see. But if the clothes were already spread out from before the Sabbath, there is no obligation to take them down. Likewise, one should not spread out a garment on the Sabbath even due to sweat. Rabbi Yosef Chaim adds, in his book Makbetzal, that the prohibition is on the very act of spreading in the manner clothes are spread after laundering — and even if one can see from a distance that the garment is dry as it is spread, people will still suspect it got a little dirty and was laundered; therefore even a completely dry garment may not be spread on the Sabbath in the manner of laundered clothes, but hanging it on a line without actually spreading it in that manner is permitted, since there is no such suspicion in that. The rule is that the prohibition is on the act of spreading itself (since at the moment people see him spreading it, they suspect he laundered it on the Sabbath), not on the garment itself; therefore, if one transgressed and spread a garment on the Sabbath anyway, even though he committed a prohibited act, there is no obligation to remove it, since removing it will not undo the suspicion already created at the time of spreading.
takeaways: It is forbidden to spread a wet garment (even slightly) to dry on the Sabbath, even in a hidden place, out of concern for suspicion of laundering — but a garment already spread from before the Sabbath need not be taken down

Even a completely dry garment may not be spread on the Sabbath in the manner of laundering (out of concern for suspicion of light soiling), but hanging it on a line without actual spreading is permitted
One who nevertheless spread a garment on the Sabbath need not remove it, since the prohibition was in the act of spreading itself

paragraphs: Begadim shemmelappepim bahem haqqetannim, nahagu haolam leshatechan beshabbat kede sheyyitnaggebu. vela mibbaya otam sheyyesh bahem likluk tzoa, deliklukan mokicha alehem shello nitkabbesu, ella gam sheen alehem likluk kelal, ella lachim hem mehashtana shehishtin hattinoq bahem, muttar leshatechan beshabbat kede sheyyitnaggebu, yaan ki begadim ellu nakerim betzuratam lekol adam shehem shel tinoqot yoneqe shadayim, vehakkol yodeim dibgadim ellu darkam lishtoach otam beli kibbus, deen mekabbesim otam ella ad sheyyarbeh liklukam beyoter, veal-ken en bahem chashad, veen limchot beyad hannohagim hetter; veayyen "maamar-mareddekay" za"l. vahagam deharab "chayye-adam" katab - tzarik iyyun beheka deen bahem likluk tzoa - hinneh katabnu taam maspiq lamminhag, veen limchot beyad hammeqillin; vehammachmir, tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: Cloths used to wrap infants — it is common practice to spread them out on the Sabbath to dry. Not only those soiled with excrement (where the soiling itself proves they were not laundered), but even those merely damp from the infant's urine, without soiling, may be spread out on the Sabbath, since these garments are recognizable to everyone as nursing infants' cloths, and everyone knows that they are normally spread out without laundering (they are laundered only when very soiled); therefore there is no suspicion at all regarding them, and one should not protest against those who follow this practice.
takeaways: It is permitted to spread wet infant cloths (even just from urine, without soiling) to dry on the Sabbath, since everyone knows these are spread out without laundering

paragraphs: Mitpechot hayyadayim shennitlachlechu harbeh merob hanniggub shenniggebu hayyadayim bahem, muttar leshatechan im nikkar bahem qetzat zuhama; veken hu haddin bemitpachat shemmeqannechin bah hachotem, deim nikkar bah likluk shel tzoat hachotem muttar lishtecha, vedame ledin begadim shemmelappepin bahem haqqetannim sheyyesh bahem likluk demuttar leshatechan. veayyen leharab "chayye-adam" b"nishmat-adam", demokicha lah min hashshulchan aruk beyoreh dea, siman p"z, gabbe mebashshel besar behema bachaleb sheqedim, deim mannicha sham sheqedim, muttar; yeuyyan sham. veken yesh lehokicha zeh gam ken missiman s"v, seip t', gabbe dam dagim, yeuyyan sham. gam harab "shem chadash", dap s", ammud b, katab lehedya din hammitpachat deshare, dedame lemah sheameru bemoed qatan, dap y"d, ammud : azoro mokicha alayv, veken bebetza, dap t', ammud : shobako mokicha alayv, yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: Hand towels that became very wet from much drying of hands may be spread out to dry if some soiling is visible on them. Likewise a handkerchief used to wipe the nose, if soiling is visible on it, may be spread out, similar to the law of soiled infant garments that may be spread out.
takeaways: A towel with a clear visible sign of soiling (sweat, mucus) may be spread out to dry on the Sabbath, since the soiling itself proves it was not laundered

paragraphs: Beged shennishra bemayim, asur letaltelo shemma yabo lide sechita. veim hu beged sheeno maqpid alayv lischatu gam bechol, kegon beged shemmesannenin bo tamid hammayim shebbechabit, o shehu parus al hammayim shebbechabit tamid, la gazerinan beh. ubeged zeh shennishra bammayim - im yetalteluhu asara bene-adam beyachad, lo gazeru bo chaza"l, mishshum demadkeri ahadade; velaken im nizdammen beged shennapal lammiqveh venashera bammayim, vechas alayv shello yishshaer bammayim ad yetziat shabbat veyitqalqel, az yabi asara bene-adam, vitiluhu veyannichuhu bemaqom acher. ubeged shennishra sheriyya muetet sheen derek lehaqpid alayv lischatu, muttar letaltelo gam hayyachid.

clarification.explanation: A garment that became wet with water may not be handled, out of concern that one might come to wring it out. But if it is a garment that people are not careful to wring out even during the week (such as cloth always used to filter water from a barrel, or cloth always placed over the water in a barrel), no decree was made about it. This wet garment, if ten people handle it together, is also not subject to the decree, since they remind each other (and will not mistakenly wring it out). Therefore, if a garment fell into a mikveh and got wet, and there is concern it will be damaged if left in the water until the conclusion of the Sabbath, ten people may be brought to take it out together and place it elsewhere. And a garment that got only slightly wet, of a kind not normally wrung out, may be handled even by a single person alone.
takeaways: A wet garment may not be handled alone, out of concern for wringing, but if ten people handle it together, this is permitted, since they remind each other not to wring it

paragraphs: Mi shennasheru kelayv bammayim beodam alayv, yakol lahalok bahem, delekka lemigzar mishshum sechita beodam alayv, ak asur lenaggebam samuk laesh apillu beodam alayv mishshum dibashshel bazeh et hammayim; veod yesh bazeh issur melabben. vekol zeh hu beheka shehu samuk laesh harbeh, shehabbeged yukal lehitchammem chimmum shehayyad soledet bo.

clarification.explanation: One whose clothes got wet while still being worn on his body may continue to walk in them, since there is no concern of wringing when the garment is worn on the body. But it is forbidden to dry them near a fire, even while still worn, since this causes "cooking" of the water in the garment, and there is also a prohibition of bleaching in this — specifically when close enough to the fire that the garment becomes hot enough to burn the hand.
takeaways: It is permitted to continue walking in a wet garment while worn, but forbidden to dry it near a fire strong enough to cause noticeable heating

paragraphs: Beged shennishra beyayin adom o shear mashqin sheenam melabbenim, muttar letaltelo apillu nishreh harbeh, dela gazerinan beh shemma yischat, dezeh hu likluk vela mehanneya leh sechita.

clarification.explanation: A garment that got wet with red wine or other beverages that do not bleach may be handled even if it got very wet, since there is no concern that one will come to wring it out — since this is a stain and not the kind of wetness for which wringing is beneficial (since wine does not clean like water).
takeaways: A garment wet with wine or a non-bleaching beverage may be handled under all circumstances, since there is no concern of wringing

paragraphs: Hamnaer tallit chadasha min hattal o min hammatar shealeha, chayyab chattat, shehanniur yapeh lah kemo kibbus. vekatebu haacharonim za"l: meachar dela yadeinan ad kamma niqra chadash, lekak yizzaher bekol gavna; veayyen "chayye-adam", seip t'. vekol zeh davqa im maqpid aleha shello yilbashenna bilti neor, abal im eno maqpid bazeh, en hanniur chashib etzlo kemo kibbus, veshare leh lenaara qodem sheyyilbashenna. veim hi lebana o adumma, en hanniur yapa lah kekibbus, velaken gam im maqpid, shari lenaara. vekol zeh davqa batel o me geshamim muatin, abal im yaredu aleha geshamim rabbim ad shennibleu bah, o shennapela letok hammayim venibleu bah hammayim harbeh, asur lenaara apillu im hi givvun laban o adom, kevan denibleu bah mayim harbeh, chosheshin lischita bishat niur, ki missetama nischatin hammayim harabbim mikkoach hanniur vekannizkar baacharonim.

clarification.explanation: One who shakes out a new tallit from dew or rain upon it is liable as one who desecrates the Sabbath (a sin-offering), since such shaking benefits it like laundering. Since one cannot know exactly until when a garment is considered "new," one must be careful in every case. All this applies specifically when one is careful not to wear the garment without shaking it out first; but if one is not careful about this, the shaking is not considered like laundering, and it is permitted to shake it before wearing. Also, if the garment is white or red, the shaking does not benefit it like laundering, and therefore it is permitted to shake it even if one is careful about it. All this applies specifically to dew or a little rainwater, but if heavy rain fell on the garment and was absorbed into it, or it fell into water and absorbed much water, it is forbidden to shake it even if it is white or red, since there is concern that shaking will cause the wringing out of the large amount of absorbed water.
takeaways: Shaking a new garment (which one is careful to shake before wearing) from dew or light rain is Torah-forbidden, like laundering — unless the garment is white/red or one is not careful about it. Since one cannot be certain when a garment stops being considered 'new,' one must be careful in every case and not rely on the assumption that it is no longer new
A garment that absorbed much water (from heavy rain or immersion) may not be shaken under any circumstances, out of concern for wringing

paragraphs: Asur lenaer beged shachor chadash min haabaq shealayv, im maqpid shello lelabesho bilti neor, mippene shezzeh hanniur hu kemo kibbus, shehaabaq meqalqel reayato. vetzarik lizzaher bazeh gam belaban ushear tzibonim, degam hem meqalqel haabaq reayatam im hu rab alehem; veayyen "mishbetzot zahab" za"l. umuttar lehasir hannotzot min beged shachor, im notzot ellu bau lo min hakkar, deenam muqtzot, ukemo shekkatab haggaon rabbenu zalman za"l; mihu, beseper hazzikronot machmir; velaken nakon lehizzaher shello lehasir shum notza mibbeged hashshachor velo shum dabar hannitleh bo.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to shake dust off a new black garment if one is careful not to wear it without shaking, since this shaking is equivalent to laundering — since the dust mars the garment's appearance. One must be careful about this also with white and other colored garments, if the dust noticeably mars them. It is permitted to remove feathers from a black garment if the feathers came from a vineyard (since they are not muktzeh), but there is a stricter opinion on this, and therefore it is correct to be careful and not remove any feather or similar object stuck to the black garment.
takeaways: Shaking dust off a new garment is forbidden if one is careful to wear it clean (since this is like laundering), and one should be careful about removing feathers stuck to a black garment as well

paragraphs: Haoseh dabar shehu gemar asiyyat keli vetiqquno, hare gemar zeh chashib melaka, vaapillu shehu dabar muat, vehu toledet "makkeh bepattish"; lepikak, halloqet yabbalto, rotzeh lemor, gabshushit sheal gabbe begadim, hannisharim min haariga, veken qashin veqesamin shenneergu babbeged shello bemitkavven, hare zeh chayyab mishshum "makkeh bepattish" im hu mesiram bekavvana kede leyappot habbeged, shehayyippuy hazzeh chashib gemar asiyyat habbeged vetiqquno; veim eno maqpid alehem veeno mesiram bekavvana kede leyappot habbeged, ella derek mitasseq bealema, nehi deissur tora lekka, mikkol maqom ikka issura middibre soperim.

clarification.explanation: One who performs an action that constitutes the completion or repair of a utensil (a garment) is considered to have performed a full act of labor (of the type "striking the final blow"), even if it is a small action. Therefore, one who deliberately removes bumps left over from the weaving process, or splinters or straw mistakenly woven into the garment, with the intention of beautifying the garment, is liable under "striking the final blow," since this beautification is considered the completion of the garment's repair. But if he is not careful about this and does not remove them intentionally to beautify it, but does so incidentally without intention, there is no Torah prohibition in this, though there is a rabbinic prohibition.
takeaways: Deliberately removing flaws (a splinter, a bump) from a garment to beautify it is Torah-forbidden; if done without special intention, it is only rabbinically forbidden

paragraphs: Im nidbaq zera pishtan o tabshil al bigdo, muttar leqallepo, kemo shekkatebu b"magen abraham" v"tosepet shabbat" verabbenu zalman za"l; vehu haddin im nidbaq bibgadayv garine temarim o shel abattichim vekayyotze, demuttar lahasiram.

clarification.explanation: If flaxseed or food residue got stuck to a garment, it is permitted to peel it off and remove it. Likewise, if date pits, watermelon seeds, or the like got stuck, it is permitted to remove them.
takeaways: It is permitted to remove food residue stuck to a garment (seeds, fruit pits, cooked food), unlike removing woven splinters meant to beautify the garment itself

paragraphs: Mi shennistabbeku begadayv beqotzim o bemasmer shebbakkotel vekayyotze, maprishan benachat ubetzina, shemmoshek otam leat leat kede shello yiqreu; vekevan shehu oseh benachat, im nizdammen shenniqra, let lan bah, deeno mitkavven lazeh, vegam la have pesiq resheh, kevan dimnatteqam benachat.

clarification.explanation: One whose clothes got caught on thorns or on a nail in a wall or the like should separate them gently and carefully, pulling slowly so they not tear. Since he does this slowly, if the garment happened to tear anyway, there is no prohibition in this, since he did not intend it, and it is also not a case of "an inevitable result" (pesik reisha), since he is detaching it gently.
takeaways: It is permitted to gently free a garment caught on a thorn or nail, and if it tears anyway there is no prohibition, since it was not done forcefully as a certain result

paragraphs: Shalal sheosin hachayyatim, shemmechabberim chatikot habbeged techilla "y tepirot gassot, veachar shettoperin otam bitpirot daqqot veyapot mesirim oto hashshalal; veim nizdammen sheshshakechu velo hesiro chut zeh shel hashshalal, asur lahasiro beshabbat, veikka issur tora im maqpid; veim lo maqpid, ikka issura derabbanan.

clarification.explanation: The basting thread tailors use (rough preliminary stitching to join pieces of cloth before the final delicate sewing), which is sometimes forgotten and left in after the sewing is finished — may not be removed on the Sabbath. If one is careful to remove it (since it protrudes or mars the appearance), there is a Torah prohibition in this; if one is not careful about it, there is a rabbinic prohibition.
takeaways: Removing a temporary basting thread forgotten after a garment's sewing is finished is forbidden on the Sabbath — a Torah prohibition if one is careful to remove it, and rabbinic if not

paragraphs: En meqappelin kelim beshabbat, ella im ken meqappelam letzorek hashshabbat, dehaynu sheyyirtzeh lelabesham achar haqqippul bo bayyom; vaapillu bazeh lo hittiru ella bimqappel adam echad, abal shene bene-adam sheyyeqappelu beyachad beged echad, asur, ki hashshenayim osim qippul yapeh umetuqqan yoter. vaapillu beadam echad lo hittiru ella bibgadim chadashim daadayin lo nitkabbesu, abal mekubbasim asur, ki haqqippul metaqqenam yoter. vaapillu chadashim lo hittiru ella bilbenim velo bitzbuim. vaapillu bilbanim lo hittiru ella raq im en lo beged echad acher mequppal lelabesho bo bayyom. vegam od bekol zeh lo hittiru ella leqappel beyado, abal al gabbe shulchan o sapsal, asur. bammeh debarim amurim? beheka shehu meqappelo bederek qippulo harishon, abal im meqappelo shello kederek qippulo harishon, muttar bekol gavna - ben bishne bene-adam, ben al hashshulchan, ben mekubbasim, ben tzebuim, ben im yesh lo acher mequppal - dekol shehu eno meqappelo beqippulo harishon, en leqippul zeh qiyyum veen kan tiqqun keli; mihu, gam bazeh eno muttar ella beheka sherotzeh lelabesho bo bayyom. v"g deharab "eliyya raba" za"l mattir gam im en dato lelabesho bo bayyom - nirin bazeh dibre harab "chayye-adam", kelal m"d, ot k"d; ukemo shekkatabti bazeh bsh"q "mqbtzl", veheeleti sham dibtallit shel tzitzit shemmeqappelo beshacharit veen lobesho bo bayyom od, yesh lismok al dibre harab "eliyya raba" leqappelo shello keseder qippulo, demishshum shehu tallit shel metzuvveh, yesh lehaqel bazeh. veyesh bene-adam shemmeqappelin tallit shel tzitzit keqippulo harishon, desomekin al sebarat h"kl bo" za"l, velo yapeh osin; deha maran za"l vekol happoseqim la nicha lehu bazeh hassebara, velaken tzarik lehizzaher betallit shel tzitzit, leqappelo beshacharit shello kederek qippulo.

clarification.explanation: One should not fold garments on the Sabbath, unless folding them for the sake of the Sabbath itself — that is, intending to wear them after folding on that same day. Even so, this is permitted only when one person folds alone, but two people folding the same garment together is forbidden, since two people produce a more precise and finished fold. Even for a single person, this is permitted only for new garments not yet laundered; laundered garments may not be folded, since folding improves them further. Even for new garments, this is permitted only for white ones, not colored ones. Even for white ones, this is permitted only if he has no other folded garment he could wear that day. And even in all this, folding is permitted only by hand, not on a table or bench. All this applies specifically when folding in the garment's usual manner, but if one folds it in a manner different from the usual fold, it is permitted in every case (even two people, even on a table, even laundered, even colored, even if there is another folded garment), since an unusual fold is not considered a permanent repair of the garment. Even this is permitted only if one intends to wear it that same day — and there is a dispute about this: Rabbi Eliyah Rabbah permits folding out of the usual order even without intending to wear it again that day, but the primary halachah follows the Chayei Adam, who permits it only when one intends to wear it that day. Regarding a tallit with tzitzit folded in the morning, with no intention of wearing it again that day — there is room to be lenient and fold it in a manner different from the usual fold, following Eliyah Rabbah's opinion, since this is a garment of a commandment. Some are accustomed to fold the tallit with tzitzit in its usual manner, relying on the Kol Bo, but Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes that this is not the correct practice, since Maran and most halachic authorities disagree with this reasoning, and therefore one should be careful to fold the tallit in the morning specifically in a manner different from its usual fold.
takeaways: Folding a garment on the Sabbath is permitted only under cumulative conditions: one person, a new unlaundered garment, white, by hand and not on a table, no other folded garment available to wear that day, and intending to wear it that same day

Folding in a manner different from the usual fold is permitted under all the other conditions (two people, a table, laundered, colored, another folded garment available), but only if one intends to wear the garment that same day; for a tallit not to be worn again that day, it is good to fold it specifically in an unusual manner
Some (mistakenly, according to most authorities and Maran) fold the tallit in its usual manner relying on the Kol Bo — the correct practice is to fold it specifically in an unusual manner

paragraphs: Kol beged leachar kibbus mitqashsheh, umeshapshepin oto beyadayim lerakkeko, v"y shipshup zeh gam hallibbun shello matzhir yoter. velaken, im hu beged elyon shehaadam maqpid yoter al libbuno sheyyatzhir, asur leshapshepo beyadayim lerakkeko, denireh kammitkavven lehatzhir hallibbun vedomeh limlabben; abal chaluq shehu beged tachton, en haadam maqpid kol kak al libbuno, umuttar leshapshepo beyadayim lerakkeko. bammeh debarim amurim? bechaluq shel tzemer o shel meshi, abal chaluq shel pishtan asur leshapshepo apillu meat beyadayim lerakkeko, mippene sherikkuko zehu lebono. vekol zeh mishshurat haddin, abal nakon lehachmir bekol chaluq "p sheeno pishtan, shello yeshapshepu kelal, mikkoach sebarat rabbenu chananel za"l disbira lah lehepek, dedavqa shel pishtan hu deshare. vekatab harab "tosepet-shabbat" dilpi zeh rauy lanu lehachmir bekol habbegadim; yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: Every garment stiffens after laundering, and is rubbed by hand to soften it, and this rubbing also makes its whiteness shine more. Therefore, an outer garment whose bright whiteness a person is more careful about may not be rubbed by hand to soften it, since this appears as an intention to brighten the whiteness and resembles the forbidden act of bleaching. But an undergarment (a robe) whose bright whiteness one is not so careful about may be rubbed by hand to soften it. This applies specifically to a wool or silk robe, but a linen robe may not be rubbed even slightly by hand to soften it, since its softening is itself its bleaching. All this is only by strict law, but in practice it is correct to be stringent about any robe and not rub it at all, since there is a dissenting opinion on this very distinction: Rabbeinu Chananel holds the opposite — that specifically a linen robe may be rubbed and not other fabrics — and in light of this dispute, Rabbi Tosefet Shabbat wrote that it is proper to be stringent and not rub any garment at all.
takeaways: An outer garment should not be rubbed by hand to soften it (this resembles bleaching); an undergarment robe may be somewhat lenient, unless it is linen

There is a dissenting opinion (Rabbeinu Chananel) holding the opposite — that specifically linen may be rubbed and not other fabrics — so in practice it is correct to be stringent and not rub any robe

paragraphs: Tit sheal raglayv o minalayv, lo yeqannechu baqqarqa, gezera shemma yabo lehashvot gummot baqqarqa; veyesh oserin leqannecho gam bekotel im hu shel binyan, mippene shennireh kemosip al habbinyan, ella yeqannechu bekotel etz o beqora. veasur leqanneach tit vekayyotze, sheal hamminal besakkin o betzipporen - ben im hamminal chadash, ben yashan - mippene shebbazeh qolep et haor vahare zeh memacheq.

clarification.explanation: Mud on the feet or shoes should not be cleaned on the ground, out of concern that one might come to level holes in the ground. Some also forbid cleaning it on a building wall, since this appears as adding to the building, but it should be cleaned on a wooden wall or beam. It is forbidden to clean mud and the like off a shoe with a knife or fingernail (whether the shoe is new or old), since this peels off the leather and is considered "scraping" (a forbidden act of labor).
takeaways: Mud on shoes should be cleaned on a wooden wall or beam (not the ground or a building wall), and not with a knife or fingernail, which peel the leather and constitute "scraping"

paragraphs: Tit sheal bigdo, lo yeshapshepu mibbachutz bimqom hattit, denireh kimlabben; ella meshapshep mibbipnim batztzad hashsheni shekkeneged hattit. veyesh omerim dehane mille betit lach, abal tit yabesh asur mippene shemmitparek, vahare zeh toledet tochen; veraq im lo yesh mammashut betit beayin ella raq mareh tit – muttar.

clarification.explanation: Mud on a garment should not be rubbed from the outside, at the place of the mud itself, since this appears like bleaching; rather it should be rubbed from the inside, from the opposite side facing the place of the mud. Some say this law applies only to wet mud, but dry mud may not be removed since it crumbles and is considered a derivative of "grinding" — and only if no noticeable substance of the mud remains, but merely a light stain, is it permitted.
takeaways: Wet mud on a garment is cleaned from the inside, not directly at the stain's location; dry mud that crumbles may not be removed at all, unless only a light stain remains

paragraphs: Beged sheyyesh alayv me raglayim o shear likluk, asur litten alayv mayim, dishriyyato zehu kibbuso, ella meqannecho bismartut benachat, velo yidchoq beqinnucha shemma yischat. veyesh oserin latet mayim apillu muatin al ezeh beged v"p sheen bo likluk, disbira lehu: sheriyyato zehu kibbuso - ayre apillu been bo likluk. ulekak, harotzeh lishtot mayim "y mappa shemmannicha al sepat hakkos, lo yaaseh zeh bachaluqo o shear beged, mishshum dishriyyato zehu kibbuso, abal bemappa hamyuchedet lekak, let lan bah, ukemo shekkatab b"chesed lealpayim" za"l.

clarification.explanation: A garment with urine stains or other filth on it — one should not pour water on it, since the soaking itself is considered like laundering; rather it should be cleaned gently with a rag, without pressing hard, lest one come to wring it. There is a stricter opinion that forbids pouring even a little water on a garment even if it has no filth at all, since in their view soaking is considered like laundering even without filth. Therefore, one who wants to drink water through a cloth placed over the rim of a cup (as a filter) should not do so with a robe or ordinary garment (out of concern for its soaking-laundering), but with a cloth specially designated for this purpose there is no concern.
takeaways: Water should not be poured on a soiled garment (the soaking itself is like laundering) — it should be cleaned gently with a rag; and for filtering drinking water, a specially designated cloth should be used, not an ordinary garment

paragraphs: Mi shennitlakleka yado battit, lo yeqannechenna bemappa shemmeqannechin bah yadayim, kede shello yabo lekabbes hammappa aach"k; ella yirchatz yadayv min hattit bemayim veaach"k yenaggebenna bemappa. v"p shemmuttar lenaggeb yadayv achar hannetila apillu bebeged shemmaqpid al memayv, mishshum dibniggub yadayim lo gazeru rabbanan kemo sheggazeru beniggub hakkos; mikkol maqom yizzaher kol adam achar sherochetz yadayv, leshapshepam techilla zo bezo bekoach kede sheyyasir hammayim shebbaayin mealehem, veaach"k yeqannechem bemappa.

clarification.explanation: One whose hand got dirty with mud should not clean it with the cloth used for drying hands, so as not to come to launder it afterward; rather he should first wash the mud off his hand with water, and only then dry his hand with the cloth. Although it is permitted to dry one's hands after washing even with a garment one is sensitive about regarding its water (since no decree was made about drying hands as there was about drying a cup), one must nevertheless be careful to first rub the hands vigorously against each other to remove the excess water before drying them with the cloth.
takeaways: A hand dirty with mud should first be washed with water and not cleaned directly with a hand towel, so as not to lead to laundering it

paragraphs: Im nitlaklek bigdo o mitpachto vekibbes beshabbat bemezid, asur lo leolam, apillu lo kibbeso kullo ella miqtzat mimmennu bimqom likluk davqa, kedin hambashshel beshabbat, dekullehu melakot shavin bedin zeh; ukemo shekkatab bitrumot, pereq b', mishna g', yeuyyan sham. ketzad yaaseh? yachzor vitannepem bechol vikabbesem, veaz muttar lehishtammesh bahem; abal lirchotz otam bechol bilti likluk, la shari behaki; ken heeleti bsh"q "rab-pealim" besiata dishmayya.

clarification.explanation: One whose garment or cloth got dirty and who deliberately (intentionally) laundered it on the Sabbath is forbidden to ever use it, even if he laundered only the soiled part, like the law of one who cooks on the Sabbath deliberately (all acts of labor are equal in this respect). What is the remedy in such a case? One deliberately soils it again and launders it normally (during the week), and then it is permitted to use; but merely washing it during the week without soiling it first does not suffice.
takeaways: A garment deliberately laundered on the Sabbath is forever forbidden for benefit, unless it is deliberately soiled again and laundered normally during the week
